story_text.value:
I built Night Shift game to make learning kubernetes easier. In this game, you are a Devops Engineer working to support your project. You will get different kind of incidents which you need to solve. You will also connect with your colleagues and face situation a normal engineer would.

This game is an attempt to make platform engineering fun and easy to learn. The game is a simulation of real world but all the logs shown are from a real cluster. I am working on another project Snowops Labs in which you can simulate real scenarios and incidents in a local cluster or GitHub codespaces. That is a bigger project but requires time to setup.

This game is just a click away to play. Just visit the url and start playing. It's totally free. You can also save your progress to change devices.

title.value: Show HN: Night Shift – A browser based incident response game

story_text.value:
After hiring engineers for the past 10 years at various startups, I realized that there were different axis of engineering preferences that impacted how well I worked with them. I decided to use Claude (sorry) to build out a quiz that ranks based on a series of questions.

It's a little cheesy, but I thought this could be a useful way to understand the style of the engineer before an interview. There aren't any "wrong" answers, just preferences, so it can't be gamed like most tests. What's good at a large company could be the opposite at a small company.

You don't need to sign up in order to take the test, so don't feel obligated.

Here is mine, as an example result https://engtest.dev/g/lucas

Would love feedback if anyone would find this useful for hiring, or if you found the results insightful!

title.value: Show HN: A Personality Test for Engineers

story_text.value:
Hi HN

I've always been drawn to puzzle and strategy games, and for a long time I've wanted to build a game of my own. While building my own version of battleship, I came across this idea of adding a super intelligent in-game AI which uses probability and statistics to reason with the board and fire its next shot.

The goal was to create a set of rules & logic capable of consistently outperforming human players, much like chess engines that have evolved to surpass even the world's strongest human chess players.

Thus I created WraithAI and named the game as Ghostfleet. WraithAI features:

1. Monte Carlo Simulation with Probability heatmaps: Before every turn WraithAI samples 800 possible enemy fleet configurations and aggregates them into a probability heatmap. It identifies the most likely locations of the enemy ships.

2. Bayesian Inference: After every shot it updates its beliefs and uses the information gain to draw a new heatmap. When two cells look equally likely WraithAI picks the one whose result would tell more about the hidden enemy fleet for its next turn.

3. Adaptive Strategy & defense: It adjusts its aggression based on the state of the game and has a mechanism which resists common search strategies.

I would genuinely like to know how people can find patterns in its behavior. Can you outsmart & beat WraithAI?

Ghostfleet also has multiplayer mode so you can play with your friends. There is a matchmaking component called TownSquare at the bottom through which you can share room codes with other players.

You can play directly in your browser:

1. Play against WraithAI: https://ghostfleet.in/play?mode=wraithAI

2. Ghostfleet: https://ghostfleet.in/

3. WraithAI Technical breakdown: https://ghostfleet.in/wraith-ai

title.value: Show HN: GhostFleet: A Battleship game with an advanced AI opponent

story_text.value:
I got Modern Combat 2: Black Pegasus running in a browser, with mouse and keyboard controls and online multiplayer.

Under the hood, a Rust ARM emulator compiled to WebAssembly runs the original Android binary.

This game used to be my childhood, playing it with my brother on the Blackberry Playbook. But it no longer ran on modern Android versions, so I thought I would port it - and even have it playable on desktop!

You'll need to bring your own APK and data file because of copyright reasons. For footage, check out my original tweet instead: https://x.com/aryanbaburajan/status/2123574545990799534
